clue.text: Man with little purpose in life

parts.note: Des is a man's name, short for Desmond
tiny means very little

explanation.surface: A rather insignificant man drifting through life without much aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man with little' reads as a description of an aimless person, but it is a name followed by a word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Destiny is what one's life is meant for, the end it is fated or intended to reach.

clue.text: Days I'm out cause concern

indicators.note: out as in out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Days off work are causing worry for the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to fill them with worry or alarm, so it means to cause concern.

clue.text: Survey shows main church member on right

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it, so this comes first

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
R is the abbreviation for right
CH abbreviates church; the word member is loose padding here

explanation.surface: A poll reveals the chief churchgoer leans to the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the high sea, a crossword favourite. R sits on top of CH in this down answer; 'member' adds nothing to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey an area is to examine it closely, which is to search it.

clue.text: Certain Latin vibe played with energy

indicators.note: played as in played about with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A Latin groove performed energetically is sure to be a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Inevitable means bound to happen and impossible to avoid, which is one sense of certain.

clue.text: Long 12 months at the Pole

parts.note: a year has twelve months
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A lengthy year spent at the North Pole, where winter nights last for months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the year but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to have an intense desire, which is what longing for something means.

clue.text: Suspicious of calls without proof of debt

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to dub is to call or name, as when knighting
an IOU (I owe you) is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of phone calls demanding money without any written evidence of what is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here has its old meaning of outside, not lacking; an IOU is a note saying 'I owe you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious describes a person who doubts or distrusts something, which is being suspicious of it.

clue.text: Sad chap returned in a hurry

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Ed is a chap's name
pressed for time means in a hurry

explanation.surface: An unhappy man comes back home rushed off his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Depressed means low in spirits, a stronger word for feeling sad.

clue.text: Exist with an insignificant amount of cash

parts.note: to be is to exist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone scrapes by on next to no money.
explanation.walkthrough: The British phrase 'not a bean' means having no money at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a bean is a tiny amount of money, as in being without a bean.

clue.text: Ingredient of a green fuel?

parts.note: olive is a shade of green
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Asks what goes into an environmentally friendly fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green fuel' suggests biofuel, but green and fuel are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is a staple cooking ingredient, used in dressings and for frying.

clue.text: It shows one the way to finish letters

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a post at a junction pointing to destinations
second meaning: read as two instructions, put your name at the end of them and then send them off

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word in two: what you do to complete a letter, then how you dispatch it.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside pointer gives directions to travellers, while signing and mailing complete correspondence.

clue.text: Rush to dispute point

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone hurries forward to argue a point in a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden flood or outpouring, a rush of something such as water or complaints.

clue.text: A very quiet part of west London seems attractive

parts.note: taken as written
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
Ealing is a district and borough in west London

explanation.surface: A peaceful corner of west London looks like a nice place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a suburb in west London, famous for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appealing draws people towards it, which is what being attractive means.

clue.text: He has lots to talk about

definitions.text: He has lots to talk about

parts.words: He has lots to talk about
parts.note: surface reading: a chatterbox with plenty of things to say
setter's reading: lots are items in a sale, which this man describes and sells off one by one

explanation.surface: A talkative man who never runs short of subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' looks like 'a great deal', but it means numbered items put up for sale in a saleroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The person conducting a sale talks through each lot in turn, taking bids until the hammer falls.

clue.text: Look sound

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a quick or furtive glance
second meaning: a weak high chirp, as from a young bird

explanation.walkthrough: 'Look sound' reads as 'seem healthy', but the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a brief glimpse, as through a keyhole, and a tiny squeak or chirp.

clue.text: Deign to be unhappily ensconced with daughter

indicators.note: unhappily suggests things going badly wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent grudgingly agrees to stay settled in at their daughter's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just adds D to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend is to do something one considers beneath one's dignity, which is what deign means.

clue.text: Partners in crime get gold that is finally theirs

parts.note: to access something is to get at or obtain it
or is gold in heraldry
i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the last letter of theirs

explanation.surface: Criminal partners grab the gold and claim it as their own at last.
explanation.walkthrough: In law an accessory is someone who helps commit a crime without being the main offender.
explanation.definitionFit: Accessories are accomplices, people who share in a crime as helpers of the principal offender.

clue.text: Family head is marked man sheltering reformed thief

indicators.note: reformed means made over in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
sheltering means protecting inside, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: in Genesis God set a mark on Cain after he killed Abel
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The clan leader is a notorious figure who protects a criminal who has gone straight.
explanation.walkthrough: Cain is the 'marked man' because of the mark of Cain in Genesis, a sign set on him after he murdered his brother.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the leader of a clan or tribe, the head of an extended family group.

clue.text: Unrealistic aspects one gets involved with

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone joins in with parts of a fanciful plan that have no grounding in reality.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapist describes fantasy that avoids reality, so an escapist view is an unrealistic one.

clue.text: Change to plain material

parts.note: small change is cash
mere means plain or nothing more than

explanation.surface: Instructions to switch to a simple, unpatterned fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like a verb but is the noun, coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, a luxury cloth.

clue.text: With little reason, man appears mean

parts.note: small means little
the mind is the seat of reason
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A man who acts without much thought comes across as petty.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-minded means petty and ungenerous in outlook, which is one sense of mean.

clue.text: Redhead and another girl turned up by chance

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of Red
taken as written

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means flipped to read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Mo is a girl's name, short for Maureen

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired woman and her friend arrived unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' reads as a ginger person, but it means the first letter of red. 'Turned up' looks like 'arrived', but in this down answer it flips MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means happening without plan or pattern, purely by chance.

clue.text: We take out OAP to new club

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: take out suggests being knocked about, so the letters are displaced into a new order

parts.note: OAP, old-age pensioner, taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A couple invite a pensioner along to a newly opened social club.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAP is an old-age pensioner. 'Club' looks like a social club, but it is a cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is a heavy stick used for hitting, so it is a weapon.

clue.text: Desperately want to be an expert within the hour

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an ace is an expert
h is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Someone longs to become a master of their craft within an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: ACE goes around H.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long or yearn for it intensely, a figurative use of feeling pain.

clue.text: Pudding with own particular fragrance

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding, the course after the main one
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A dessert that comes with its own distinctive smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Afters is a British informal word for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is a scented lotion men apply after shaving, a specific kind of fragrance.

clue.text: More to come from old-time artist

parts.note: ex means former or old
t is the abbreviation for time
RA, Royal Academician, is a stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist from a bygone age promises further work is on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-time' looks like one adjective but splits into old and time.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, an amount more than what was there before.

clue.text: Pointlessly mock non-alcoholic drinks

indicators.note: pointlessly is read as without a point, so a compass point letter is dropped

parts.note: to tease is to mock playfully

explanation.surface: Someone ridicules soft drinks for no good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E (east, a compass point) is removed from TEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Teas are hot infused drinks containing no alcohol.

clue.text: In a gentle fashion, is unsophisticated

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Behaving in a mild, gentle manner is dismissed as lacking polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a gentle fashion' reads as 'gently', but fashion is the signal to rearrange the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace or refinement, so it describes something crude or unsophisticated.

clue.text: Finish ahead on purpose

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it, so the word after this one goes first

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
up means ahead, as a team two goals up

explanation.surface: Someone deliberately finishes in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead on purpose' sounds like 'early, deliberately', but each word is a separate piece and 'on' sets their order.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up is to finish or finally arrive somewhere, often without having planned it.

clue.text: They first argue it's a crime against the state

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of They
to reason is to argue a case logically

explanation.surface: Plotters debate a scheme and claim their action is an offence against the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country, such as plotting to overthrow its ruler or government.

clue.text: Stomach upset? Bad sign!

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: An upset stomach is taken as a bad omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' attaches to 'Stomach' in the surface, but it signals rearranging the word that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdomen is the belly region of the body containing the stomach, so the two are loosely interchangeable.
